I found the paper you're looking for! Here are the key details:

**DsDm: Model-Aware Dataset Selection with Datamodels** was published in the Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2024), by Logan Engstrom, Axel Feldmann, and Aleksander Mădry from MIT.

The paper addresses the problem that selecting data according to similarity with "high quality" data sources may not increase (and can even hurt) performance compared to randomly selecting data. 

The authors frame dataset selection as an optimization problem: given target tasks, a learning algorithm, and candidate data, select the subset that maximizes model performance. Their method, DsDM (dataset selection with datamodels), consistently improves language model performance on diverse target tasks like SQuAD and LAMBADA.

The paper is available on arXiv (2401.12926) and in the ICML 2024 proceedings.

Early data curation relied on perplexity filtering to approximate quality~\citep{wenzek2020ccnet}; recent methods optimize composition at the domain level via DRO~\citep{oren2019dro,xie2023doremi}, importance sampling~\citep{xie2023dsir,grangier2025crisp}, or mixing laws~\citep{ye2025mixing}, and at the instance level via deduplication~\citep{abbas2023semdedup}, curriculum strategies~\citep{bengio2009curriculum,mindermann2022prioritized}, loss-based reweighting~\citep{sow2025dynamic}, perplexity correlations~\citep{thrush2025perplexity}, or model-aware selection~\citep{engstrom2024dsdm}; see \citet{albalak2024survey} for a survey.
These methods use loss, frequency, quality, or domain membership as the selection signal---and classifier-based quality scores may not capture a meaningful quality notion~\citep{naitsaada2025illusion}---but none targets synthetic provenance.

1	\paragraph{Synthetic Contamination and Model Collapse.}
2	Training on recursively generated data leads to irreversible quality degradation (\emph{model collapse})~\citep{shumailov2024model}.
3	\citet{alemohammad2024mad} formalize this as Model Autophagy Disorder, showing that quality inevitably degrades without fresh real data.
4	More critically, \citet{dohmatob2025strong} prove under scaling-law regimes that even a vanishingly small synthetic fraction suffices to trigger collapse, ruling out data scaling as a remedy.
5	\citet{cheng2025contamination} confirm that synthetic content now constitutes an estimated 20--60\% of web corpora; whether this causes collapse depends on the data workflow---accumulating real data alongside synthetic avoids divergence~\citep{kazdan2025collapse}, and even minimal curation suffices for continual improvement~\citep{amin2025escaping}.
6	Not all synthetic data is harmful: the Phi series~\citep{gunasekar2023textbooks,li2023textbooks2} demonstrates that curated synthetic data can improve training efficiency, but this assumes intentional generation with quality control, unlike the uncontrolled web contamination we address.
7	
8	\paragraph{Detection, Filtering, and Data Reweighting.}
9	Multiple detectors produce continuous scores suitable for downstream weighting: DetectGPT~\citep{mitchell2023detectgpt} uses probability curvature, Binoculars~\citep{hans2024binoculars} cross-perplexity ratios, and Min-$k$\% Prob~\citep{shi2024minkprob} low-probability token statistics; \citet{wu2025survey} survey the broader detection landscape.

Early data curation relied on perplexity filtering to approximate quality~\citep{wenzek2020ccnet}; recent methods optimize composition at the domain level via DRO~\citep{oren2019dro,xie2023doremi}, importance sampling~\citep{xie2023dsir,grangier2025crisp}, or mixing laws~\citep{ye2025mixing}, and at the instance level via deduplication~\citep{abbas2023semdedup}, curriculum strategies~\citep{bengio2009curriculum,mindermann2022prioritized}, loss-based reweighting~\citep{sow2025dynamic}, perplexity correlations~\citep{thrush2025perplexity}, or model-aware selection~\citep{engstrom2024dsdm}; see \citet{albalak2024survey} for a survey.
These methods use loss, frequency, quality, or domain membership as the selection signal---and classifier-based quality scores may not capture a meaningful quality notion~\citep{naitsaada2025illusion}---but none targets synthetic provenance.
tool_args.new_text:
A parallel line of work optimizes data composition via perplexity filtering~\citep{wenzek2020ccnet}, domain-level DRO or importance sampling~\citep{oren2019dro,xie2023doremi,xie2023dsir,grangier2025crisp,ye2025mixing}, and instance-level strategies including curriculum learning~\citep{bengio2009curriculum,mindermann2022prioritized}, deduplication~\citep{abbas2023semdedup}, loss-based reweighting~\citep{sow2025dynamic}, perplexity correlations~\citep{thrush2025perplexity}, or model-aware selection~\citep{engstrom2024dsdm}; see \citet{albalak2024survey} for a survey.
None targets synthetic provenance; moreover, classifier-based quality scores may capture stylistic similarity rather than intrinsic quality~\citep{naitsaada2025illusion}.
